q: what is the difference between == and === in js
double equals vs triple equals javascript
a: == is loose equality: it converts the operands to a common type before comparing, so 5 == '5' is true and 0 == false is true. === is strict equality: it compares both value AND type without conversion, so 5 === '5' is false and 0 === false is false. Always prefer === (and !==) to avoid surprising type-coercion bugs. The only cases where == is deliberately used are checking for both null and undefined at once: value == null is true for both null and undefined.
code:
console.log(5 == '5');    // true  (coerces)
console.log(5 === '5');   // false (type differs)
console.log(0 == false);   // true
console.log(0 === false);  // false
console.log(null == undefined);   // true
console.log(null === undefined);  // false

// Safe null check
if (value == null) { /* null OR undefined */ }
